source.title: FlowAdam: Implicit Regularization via Geometry-Aware Soft Momentum Injection

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; some PDF extraction artifacts are present, but the relevant results and tables are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Introduces a different optimizer and reports held-out performance across coupled and well-conditioned tasks, extending generalization comparisons to these settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own held-out benchmark results for FlowAdam and comparison optimizers. It does not test the specific claim versions about random-label memorization, width, convolutional architecture, Adam versus SGD generalization, batch size, dropout, sharpness measures, or removing memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The paper evaluates FlowAdam against other optimizers but tests none of V1–V8. In particular, its held-out comparisons lack SGD or momentum SGD, so they do not test V4. SGD appears only in training-accuracy and optimization-loss diagnostics. Generalization improvements over Adam alone do not establish a listed claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: they attribute FlowAdam's gains on coupled workloads to implicit regularization from its ODE trajectory and report parity on CIFAR-10 and residualized MovieLens. Their claimed mechanism confirmation should remain an attribution: MovieLens parity and the compute controls are consistent with that explanation but do not establish it uniquely. The authors also emphasize soft momentum injection as essential to avoiding hybrid-training instability.
record.recipe_differences: A hybrid Adam and clipped ODE-gradient-flow optimizer with adaptive switching and soft momentum injection; the reported benchmarks are not reproductions of the cited studies' methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that coupling and conditioning affect whether FlowAdam improves results: it improves results on the coupled benchmarks but matches Adam on CIFAR-10 and residualized MovieLens. They also report sensitivity to switching threshold αs, injection weight γ, and full-batch versus mini-batch noise.

fits_no_version.finding: FlowAdam improves reported errors over Adam on matrix/tensor recovery and Jester and improves GNN AUC, while matching Adam on CIFAR-10 and residualized MovieLens.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hybrid Adam–ODE optimization can improve held-out performance over Adam in some tested coupled, low-noise workloads.

fits_no_version.finding: On Jester, Adam at 4,350 gradient evaluations has test RMSE 5.007, versus 4.731 at 1,000 steps and FlowAdam's 4.427.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Extending Adam to the reported matched compute budget does not recover FlowAdam's Jester performance.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Joint Conference on Neural Network (as stated in supplied metadata)
record.problems: Evaluation is limited to small- and medium-scale benchmarks, as the authors state; mini-batch noise limits reliable ODE triggering. Several results concern synthetic or specialized tasks. The paper gives mean ± std over 5 seeds for most experiments; no formal significance tests are stated.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports additional optimizer comparisons and sensitivity figures, as well as Rosenbrock loss and two-spirals accuracy, but these do not add held-out generalization outcomes relevant to the claim beyond the retained benchmark rows. Table VII contains tuned method comparisons on Jester; those values are not extracted because they use a different tuning protocol and do not test one of the mapped claim versions.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization alongside natural-label generalization and chance held-out performance on random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, local connectivity, and initialization effects.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under limited or broader tuning, decoupled-weight-decay recovery, Adam-to-SGD switching, and word-level language models.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that change the large-batch penalty.
Dropout effects, training-set-size dependence, excessive dropout, and joint dropout/weight-decay removal with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, generalization-gap rankings, and comparison with norm or margin measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and measuring retrained test accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's tests/T3 classification to discusses/T6. R1–R32 are optimizer benchmark or control results outside the listed versions, rather than claim-evidence rows. References to Wilson et al. and AdamW do not themselves test V4. No missing results bearing on V1–V8 were found in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and test performance on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD under limited and broader tuning; switching from Adam to SGD; word-level language models.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
